coaching.headline: GRIM.exe's twelve kills, six on Steel, and an enemy sweep of every Fangtooth and Seedling decided the game before the Core fell.

flags.text: GRIM.exe went 12/5/7 with 40% of enemy kills: six on Steel, three on Countess, two on Wraith.
Enemy took every damn pit objective: three Seedlings, three Fangtooths, Primal Fangtooth; Kwang took six.
Wraith died eleven times, the game's most: four to Kwang, three outside any detected fight.
Lost 1-4 at the Fangtooth pit; Primal Fangtooth, an inhibitor and the Core fell within a minute.

focus.title: Pop the shield, then fight the pit
focus.action: Before contesting Fangtooth, the team groups at the pit, baits GRIM.exe's Energy Shield with a cheap ability, then chains Steel's Shield Slam into Sevarog's Subjugate before Countess commits Feast.

2.7.call: Lost 0-3 on the duo lane in the allied half: GRIM.exe took first blood on Wraith, then Riktor killed Serath and Kwang killed Steel. When Kwang shows on the duo lane early, the allied duo gives ground.

19.2.call: Won 2-0: Countess killed Neon in the allied jungle and Sevarog killed Kwang on the offlane, yet the allied offlane outer fell next and the win brought no prize. With Kwang dead, push an enemy tower together.

26.1.call: Won 3-1 on the duo lane in the enemy half: Serath killed GRIM.exe, Wraith killed Riktor, razed the enemy duo outer and killed Neon, then Kwang killed Wraith. Cashed; after the third kill the carry backs off.

29.2.call: Two separate plays: GRIM.exe killed Steel, Wraith and Countess on mid, and Sevarog killed Scarlett on the offlane; the allied mid inner and mid inhibitor fell after. Against a fed GRIM.exe, mid fights wait for Sevarog.

31.2.call: Lost 1-4 at the Fangtooth pit: Kwang killed Wraith first, then GRIM.exe killed Countess and Steel and Kwang killed Sevarog; Countess took Scarlett down. After the first death at the pit, concede Primal Fangtooth and hold the base.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Nine deaths against an own average of four, six to GRIM.exe, two before minute ten. When Energy Shield is up, bait the block with Shield Bash before Shield Slam.
Game-high 15 wards above an own average of 11.9, plus 7534 healing, but just 35% kill participation. When Wraith fights on the duo lane, stay in range to follow up.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: All three deaths went to GRIM.exe, one on the duo lane outside any detected fight. Before Feast on GRIM.exe, spend Eventide first to pop Energy Shield.
Four kills, including Riktor on the duo lane the same second Riktor killed Serath. When the duo lane fights and mid is quiet, keep making that rotation.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: One death all game, the fewest of all ten, and the most mitigated damage among allies at 49980. In grouped fights, hold Subjugate for Kwang or Scarlett diving Wraith.
Two rotation kills on Neon at mid, neither followed by an allied prize. After the next rotation kill, hit the mid tower with the midlaner before heading home.
0315e661-4bc0-4b77-a997-e1d4bda2b060: Eleven deaths, every enemy hero scoring at least one and Kwang the most. When Kwang is unseen, walk the duo lane only beside Steel or Serath.
Game-high 59047 hero damage, 1845 per minute against an own average of 1152, plus the enemy duo outer. After a won fight, back off while Kwang lives.
6529fa15-498b-418d-99bb-e8743ea5cf4c: Three of four kills landed on GRIM.exe, the enemy's top killer, plus seven assists. Keep hunting GRIM.exe on the duo lane whenever Riktor is dead or shown elsewhere.
Zero of seven pit objectives, and a death to Kwang at the Fangtooth pit preceded Kwang's first Fangtooth. Before the next Fangtooth, bring Steel or Sevarog to the pit.

matchup: Duo was Wraith and this support against GRIM.exe and Riktor; allied duo deaths before minute ten ran three to none.
GRIM.exe dealt 44862 magical damage to heroes and only 442 physical.
build: Forticus and Fire Blossom both add physical armor; Raiment of Renewal adds health and out-of-combat regeneration.
Took 44828 magical hero damage against 6516 physical, so the physical armor guarded the smaller share.
Fire Blossom, finished last, was absent from every fight before the final one at the Fangtooth pit.
eternal: Krix adds max health and size; Regenerative Tissue regenerates away from hero damage, Cannibalism adds health per takedown.
Knell leans ahead in this support Eternal field; Krix, the most played, ranks well behind.
augment: Heavy Metal adds magical damage on Heavy Punches and Shield Bash, scaled by total physical and magical armor.
Heavy Metal leads a toss-up with Adaptive Force in this support augment field.
crest: Sanctification's Safeguard shields nearby heroes and grants tenacity while the shield holds; Visionary raises the ward cap.
Leafsong clearly leads this support crest field; Sanctification, the most played, ranks behind Rift Walkers too.
improvement: Build notes show the 61% core of Dynamo, Tainted Charm and Xenia went entirely unbuilt.
If GRIM.exe leads the enemy damage again, a magical armor item over Fire Blossom also feeds Heavy Metal, losing the burn aura.
Leafsong over Sanctification is the field-backed crest swap: ally speed and slow immunity instead of the Safeguard shield.

matchup: Mid opponent was Neon; Neon died four times, once to this midlaner and twice to Sevarog rotations.
GRIM.exe, not Neon, scored all three kills on this midlaner; Energy Shield blocks the next enemy ability.
Neon razed the allied offlane inner and the offlane inhibitor late.
build: Combustion, Noxia and Overseer are the full 58.4% winning core.
Overseer, finished last, adds Feast damage and heals for a share of Feast damage on heroes.
No item or the crest adds armor of either type.
eternal: Lotus grants random damage, haste, speed or health over time and on takedowns; Flawless heals nearby allies on ability hits.
Lotus leads a toss-up with Aion in this midlane Eternal field.
Fragrance adds magical and true damage against nearby enemy heroes.
augment: Sanguine Slash makes Blade Siphon hit harder and heal more against isolated targets.
Shadow Echo leads a toss-up with Blood Well in this midlane augment field; Sanguine Slash ranks third.
crest: Tempest's Overcharge burns up to three nearby heroes for several seconds and heals for a share of the damage.
Voidgazer leans ahead of Tempest in this midlane crest field.
improvement: Build notes flag GRIM.exe as the repeat killer with no armor built; GRIM.exe's damage was magical.
If GRIM.exe runs the game again, swap Tainted Scepter for a magical armor item, giving up the anti-heal.
Voidgazer over Tempest is the field lean: a slowing skillshot instead of Overcharge's area damage and healing.

matchup: Offlane opponent was Scarlett, a 45.5% lane on paper; Scarlett died once to this offlaner and never killed back.
Scarlett's Swan Song roots and is unstoppable, so crowd control will not stop Swan Song.
build: Forticus and Tainted Guard are two of the 62.5% winning core; Fire Blossom never made the build.
Tainted Guard cuts a basic attacker's healing and bleeds the attacker, a fit into Scarlett's 28242 physical damage.
Flux Matrix, finished last, adds magical armor; earlier fights lacked Flux Matrix.
eternal: Nihil grows power and armor while damaging heroes; From the Abyss heals in hero combat, Adaptive Plating adds matching armor.
Nihil clearly leads this offlane Eternal field.
augment: Grim Harvest makes Siphon execute enemies below a small health threshold.
Unholy Pursuit clearly leads this offlane augment field over Grim Harvest.
crest: Razorback's Echidna active raises both armor types briefly and reflects a share of hero damage taken.
Saphir's Mantle leads a toss-up with Nyr Warboots in this offlane crest field; Razorback ranks behind both.
improvement: Into Scarlett the field buys Fire Blossom 75% of the time against a usual 62%, completing the winning core.
Unholy Pursuit over Grim Harvest is the field-backed augment swap, giving up the Siphon execute.

matchup: Duo was this carry and Steel against GRIM.exe and Riktor; GRIM.exe out-earned this carry 17346 gold to 15386.
Kwang scored four of eleven deaths; Kwang's Surge of the Heavens knocks up and stuns, Riktor's Skewer suppresses.
build: None of the 65.1% core of Alternator, Vanquisher and Tainted Trident made the build.
Demolisher ignores physical armor only, so the magical Knock, Knock! from Mystic Marksman gains nothing from Demolisher.
Necrosis adds ultimate haste; Back It Up! lists no damage, so the ultimate damage bonus goes unused.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles after damaging a hero below a health threshold; Taproot heals on basic attacks.
Lotus clearly leads this carry Eternal field; Weald ranks well behind.
augment: Mystic Marksman turns Knock, Knock! into magical damage; 13847 of the hero damage dealt was magical.
Sniper's Bounty leans ahead in this carry augment field; Mystic Marksman ranks last of three.
crest: Pacifier's Adrenalize dashes and empowers the next physical hit, much stronger on low-health targets, with a recast on hero kills.
Witchstalker leans ahead in this carry crest field; Pacifier ranks well behind.
improvement: If GRIM.exe stacks lifesteal again, Tainted Trident from the 65.1% core over Demolisher cuts that healing, losing armor penetration.
Sniper's Bounty over Mystic Marksman is the field-backed augment swap, giving up the magical Knock, Knock!.

matchup: Kwang, the jungle opponent, killed this jungler twice and took six of seven pit objectives.
Gank targets: three kills on GRIM.exe and one on Riktor, all on the duo lane.
build: Sky Splitter and Storm Breaker are two of the 65.1% winning core; Tainted Rounds never made the build.
Sky Splitter's basic attacks deal a share of the target's current health, useful into Riktor's game-high 91930 mitigated damage.
Absolution, finished last, adds magical armor and tenacity; every fight ran without Absolution.
eternal: Vermis adds max-health damage on every third basic attack; Serration adds missing-health damage, Melting Point hits high-armor targets harder.
Weald leads a toss-up with Xyris in this jungle Eternal field; Vermis ranks well behind.
augment: Crushing Descent makes Ascend stun briefly on damage.
Crushing Descent leans ahead in this jungle augment field.
crest: Eviscerator's Rending Strikes active adds attack speed, omnivamp and on-hit damage.
Liberator clearly leads this jungle crest field; Eviscerator, the most played, ranks behind.
improvement: Tainted Rounds completes the 65.1% core and cuts healing on basic-attack hits, into Kwang's 9432 healing.
Liberator over Eviscerator is the field-backed crest swap: a cleanse and shield instead of the attack-speed burst.

threats: Chain-CC risk (4 hard-CC abilities, ~3.0s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s), Kwang Surge of the Heavens (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Riktor. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
Enemy is 4/5 magical — one magic-resist item goes a long way.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Peekaboo! to mark, reveal and slow → Knock, Knock! snipe on the marked target → Back It Up! to drag a fleeing hero back
ourKits.winCondition: land Knock, Knock! on Peekaboo!-marked targets for max-health damage and reset Surprise, Surprise! on takedowns
ourKits.passive: his vision item becomes a camouflaged Sonar Drone that reveals enemies through walls
ourKits.playWith: engage that holds targets still for his snipe, and teammates who follow up when Back It Up! returns a hero
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Peekaboo! since Knock, Knock! is much stronger on marked targets; after Back It Up! teleports you back, expect a follow-up, and pressure him after Surprise, Surprise! is spent

ourKits.combo: Phantom Rush to fly through and fear enemies, Subjugate to chain them in place, Siphon to steal max health, then Colossal Blow to knock them back.
ourKits.winCondition: Farm Souls with ability last hits to reach his tiers, then lock fights with fear and Subjugate while Siphon makes him tankier.
ourKits.passive: Reaper of Souls: ability kills give Souls for bonus health, with tiers adding omnivamp, a magical armor shred aura, stronger Siphon and damage reflect.
ourKits.playWith: A team that turns his fear and Subjugate lockdown into kills.
ourKits.playAgainst: Do not walk out of Subjugate while chained, since leaving stuns you; wait it out. Contest his last hits early to slow his Souls, and position so Colossal Blow cannot knock you into his team.

ourKits.combo: Shadow Slip dashes in, Eventide and Blade Siphon hit to apply Haemorrhage, then Feast suppresses the Haemorrhaged target for bonus damage and full healing, with Shadow Slip recast to swap back out
ourKits.winCondition: Feast a Haemorrhaged squishy for bonus damage, heal it back, and escape through the Shadow swap
ourKits.passive: hitting a hero with two abilities within a short window applies Haemorrhage, a max-health true-damage bleed
ourKits.playWith: a team to clean up after her pick
ourKits.playAgainst: Feast is her engage, so peel or punish after it is spent; note where her Shadow was left, since she can swap back to it; magic armor and anti-heal blunt her Blade Siphon and Feast healing

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush in unstoppable to knock back → Shield Bash stun → Shield Slam knockup and stun, Force Shield to block projectiles
ourKits.winCondition: engage with Shield Slam or Bull Rush and protect carries with Force Shield's projectile wall
ourKits.passive: a self-shield that lasts until broken and refreshes when out of damage, plus hybrid armor
ourKits.playWith: ranged carries he can shield from enemy projectiles, and follow-up damage for his engages
ourKits.playAgainst: Bull Rush is unstoppable, so do not waste CC into it; walk around Force Shield instead of shooting into it, and fight after Shield Slam is on cooldown

ourKits.combo: Ascend to dive onto the backline, Chastise to slow and reset her basic attack, Heaven's Fury to go untargetable and strike, then Heresy for speed, attack speed and true-damage burns.
ourKits.winCondition: Dive the backline, get the first takedown and chain free Heresy activations from Fallen Grace.
ourKits.passive: Fallen Grace: hero takedowns drop a visage that, when touched, activates Heresy for free and cuts her basic ability cooldowns.
ourKits.playWith: A frontline that creates her dive angle and CC that holds targets for her.
ourKits.playAgainst: Do not waste CC or burst during Heaven's Fury, since she is invulnerable then; hit her as she lands from Ascend. Deny the first kill so she cannot pick up the visage.

enemyKits.combo: First Intent dash in for a shield, Ashen Vow outer edge to slow and empower Cindara, Swan Song to restrain the target and set her blade Ablaze, then Minueta stabs to execute.
enemyKits.winCondition: Land Swan Song on a key target to restrain them and spend the Ablaze window with longer range and more power, finishing with Minueta.
enemyKits.passive: Last Light: she uses Energy instead of Mana, restores Energy on takedowns, and turns bonus mana into physical power.
enemyKits.playWith: Engage or CC teammates who group enemies for Ashen Vow and help her reach the restrained target.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Ashen Vow has a short channel and its slow is on the outer edge, so step inside or away. She is Unstoppable during Swan Song, so save CC for after it; fight her after First Intent's shield is spent. Armor answers her physical damage.

enemyKits.combo: Riplash to pull a hero in, Shock Therapy to break their shield and silence, Electrocute aura for damage and a shield, then Skewer to suppress everyone in front of him.
enemyKits.winCondition: Land Riplash and chain silence and suppress so the target cannot fight back while their cooldowns stay frozen.
enemyKits.passive: Suspended Sentence: while his abilities immobilize or silence a hero, their cooldowns stop ticking.
enemyKits.playWith: Burst that deletes his pulled or suppressed target.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Stay behind minions or spaced so Riplash cannot reach you, and fight while it is on cooldown. Tenacity shortens the chain, which also shortens the cooldown freeze.

enemyKits.combo: Energy Shield to block an incoming ability, Assault Mode for long-range cleaving basics, Displacement Blast to push enemies away, GTFO to finish a fleeing target.
enemyKits.winCondition: Out-trade with Pulsefire true damage and long-range Assault Mode basics, then chase kills across the map with GTFO.
enemyKits.passive: Pulsefire makes his basics deal magical damage and his next basic or ability bursts a mark for true damage.
enemyKits.playWith: Frontliners who peel and keep divers off him while he shoots from range.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Bait Energy Shield with a cheap ability, then land your real CC. GTFO is blocked by enemy heroes, so a teammate can body-block it for a low target; dive him while he is slowed channeling it.

enemyKits.combo: Judgement of the Heavens to tether, Surge of the Heavens into the Blade to knock up and stun, Light of the Heavens for true damage at the Blade, Fury of the Heavens to teleport and slow.
enemyKits.winCondition: Tether a target with the Blade, knock them up by dashing into it, and brawl with Energized basics that cut his cooldowns.
enemyKits.passive: Strike of the Heavens Energizes his basics after ability hits, adding attack speed, lightning damage and cooldown reduction.
enemyKits.playWith: Follow-up damage while he tethers and knocks up.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Watch where the Blade lands: it tethers, Surge into it knocks up, and Fury teleports him to it. Move away from the Blade and fight after Surge is used.

enemyKits.combo: Cast basic abilities to build 3 Thread, then Overclock Data Burst to slow and Mesmerize, follow with L.I.N.X true damage and an Erase Vector dash into the exploding Jolt; Final Thread Overclocks everything and its recast bomb finishes low targets.
enemyKits.winCondition: Chunk enemies with Overclocked abilities in lane and teamfights, then use Final Thread to chain several Overclocked casts and execute with the bomb.
enemyKits.passive: Neural Network: every 3 basic ability casts Overclock her next basic ability for an extra effect.
enemyKits.playWith: Frontliners or engage supports who keep enemies in Data Burst range and give her time to cycle Thread.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Watch her Thread count and respect the next ability when she is at 3, since Overclocked Data Burst Mesmerizes. Dodge the lobbed Data Burst before it detonates, and engage after Erase Vector is spent, which is her only dash. Magic armor helps but L.I.N.X return and pulse are true damage.

Necrosis (Matter Disruptor): Your Ultimate Ability deals 15% more damage.
Wraith dealt 59,047 hero damage, 42% of their team's, with +190 physical power from items.

Penetration: Demolisher ignores 25%; against GRIM.exe (level 17 estimated: about 117 physical armor, 88 after penetration) and Riktor (level 17 estimated: about 267 physical armor, 201 after penetration) that is about 16% and 22% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Scattershot (item): Upon successful On-Hit Attack: Summon 2 projectiles from the Target. These home towards the closest Enemies. Each deals (+40%) Damage. Applies On-Hit effects at 50% effectiveness.
Lightning Hawk (item): While moving or landing Basic Attacks: Generate stacks of Momentum. At 100 stacks empower your next Basic Attack On-Hit. Deal 40 (+20%) Damage. Slows by 20% for 0.75s.
Necrosis (item): Your Ultimate Ability deals 15% more damage.

Lesson: Wraith's penetration cut through: GRIM.exe took about 16% more physical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 17 (estimated) their armor was about 117, about 88 after 25% penetration).
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Scattershot, Lightning Hawk, Demolisher.
Countered? 1 of the 4 players Wraith killed built physical armor (Riktor). Anti-heal on GRIM.exe, Kwang. We killed Wraith 11 times.
Copy it? Too few Wraith carry games with this Eternal or core this patch to say whether it wins elsewhere.

bullets: Assault Mode basic attacks applied Pulsefire, and the next hit burst Pulsefire for true damage; Tainted Rounds added on-hit damage that grows as the target's health drops.
Xyris bonus damage grew with units killed, up to a cap, and Bone Collector adds permanent critical chance after enough kills, which Assault Mode's bonus damage can use.
Iron Will restored health from basic attack damage, more on critical strikes, while Tainted Rounds cut the target's healing on basic attacks.
Basic attacks built Lightning Hawk's Momentum toward an empowered, slowing shot, while Scattershot, on an internal cooldown, sent extra projectiles from the target to the closest enemies.
Weald fires true damage missiles when Wraith damages an enemy hero below the health threshold, on a per-hero cooldown; more bonus attack speed adds more missiles.
Taproot restored health on basic attack hits, scaling with bonus physical power, and Forage added extra gold and experience per minion or monster kill.
Knell's Rust from attacks and abilities shredded enemy heroes' armors and gave Riktor most of that armor; Peal added ultimate haste and briefly maxed Rust after Skewer.
Patina's shield after a stretch without damage and Forticus's shield on taking hero damage, on cooldown, both feed Transference, returning part of an expiring shield as health.
Shock Therapy's silence froze the target's cooldowns through Suspended Sentence, and immobilizing heroes with Skewer set off Vortex Stone's shield and basic ability cooldown cut.
Vesh added a damage-over-time slice to Kwang's ability damage on heroes, Lich healed Kwang off magical damage, and Millennia raised Fury of the Heavens damage every minute.
Ability hits energized the Heavenly Blade for attack speed and a lightning strike, and Oathkeeper, on a short cooldown, empowered a basic attack within 4s of a cast.
Tainted Scepter cut healing on targets hit by magical damage and built Malice stacks, filled instantly by takedowns, adding damage to ability hits on heroes.

coachLean.headline: Every pit objective went to the enemy, and two inhibitors fell right after the last two fights, lost 1-3 and 1-4.

flags.text: All three Fangtooths went to the enemy, two with no ally dead in the prior 60 seconds.
GRIM.exe went 12/5/7 with 48559 hero damage, almost all magical, for 40% of the enemy's kills.
Steel died 9 times against an own average of 4, with 6 deaths to GRIM.exe.
Wraith's 59047 hero damage led the game: 1845 a minute against an own average of 1152.

focus.action: Arrive at each Fangtooth together, bait GRIM.exe's Energy Shield with a cheap ability, then open with Shield Slam and chain Subjugate and Feast onto GRIM.exe.

0315e661-4bc0-4b77-a997-e1d4bda2b060: Eleven deaths, the most in the game, four to Kwang; next game, wait out Surge of the Heavens before committing to basic attacks.
Duo lane gave up first blood and 3 deaths to 0 before minute 10; next fight, follow Feast's suppress with Knock, Knock! for the pick.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Died once while mitigating 49980 damage and placing 11 wards; next teamfight, land Subjugate as Shield Slam ends.
Twice killed Neon on the mid lane before the enemy offlane opened; the second trip ended 1-1 when Steel died to Scarlett.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: All 3 deaths went to GRIM.exe; next game, let a teammate bait Energy Shield before committing Feast.
Took Neon in the skirmish won 2-0 with Sevarog, then Riktor and Kwang back to back, plus 5304 objective damage.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Ran the vision: 15 wards against an own average of 11.9, plus 2 cleared, alongside 35% kill participation and 7534 healing.

6529fa15-498b-418d-99bb-e8743ea5cf4c: Led the team with 65% kill participation, and 90 of 206 jungle minions came from the enemy side.
Zero wards placed and 1 cleared; if wards were equipped but unused, ward the Fangtooth pit before each spawn next game.
